title: HPE wins $2B contract with the NSA
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) has secured a 10-year, $2 billion contract with the National Security Agency (NSA). This agreement involves the NSA leveraging HPE's high-performance computing technology through the HPE GreenLake platform. HPE will build and manage a comprehensive HPC solution, encompassing HPE Apollo systems and HPE ProLiant servers, capable of processing vast amounts of data and supporting AI capabilities, to be hosted in a QTS data center and operational by 2022.

title: 7 Robotics Stocks to Buy for Elon Musk’s Big ‘Tesla Bot’ Bet
summary: This article highlights seven robotics stocks that are poised for lucrative returns, driven by the increasing demand for robotics across various industries and tech giants like Tesla and Amazon. It discusses the market growth projections for industrial robotics and provides detailed analysis, financial data, and future outlook for each recommended stock, including ABB, AeroVironment, Global X Robotics & Artificial Intelligence ETF, Intuitive Surgical, iRobot, Oceaneering International, and Raytheon Technologies. The author emphasizes that these companies leverage automation and AI to enhance efficiency and address evolving market needs.

title: Amazon reveals plans to hire 55,000 corporate and tech workers
summary: Amazon plans to hire 55,000 new corporate and tech employees worldwide, with 40,000 in the U.S., focusing on e-commerce, cloud computing, and online advertising divisions. This hiring surge, announced ahead of its Career Day 2021, will also expand its satellite internet business and increase its corporate and tech workforce by 20%. The company continues to invest in new office spaces and logistics facilities to support its rapid growth.

title: Discover More VM-Series Efficiency with Amazon Web Services VPC More Specific Routing
summary: Palo Alto Networks announced that its VM-Series virtual firewalls now integrate with the new Amazon Web Services VPC More Specific Routing feature. This integration enhances security efficiency by allowing seamless insertion of VM-Series firewalls to protect intra-VPC traffic and improves visibility for internet egress traffic from private subnets. This development makes it easier to deploy secure production-grade applications and strengthens overall security posture in AWS cloud environments.

title: Focus: Amazon's new union battle: Teamsters go local to snarl expansion
summary: The Teamsters Union is shifting its strategy to combat Amazon's expansion by focusing on local government challenges to derail new projects and calling for better labor standards. This approach follows an unsuccessful attempt by another union to organize Amazon workers in Alabama, indicating a long-term strategy of disruption rather than immediate unionization. The Teamsters are leveraging their local networks, community groups, and financial resources to pressure Amazon in specific municipalities across the U.S.

title: AWS, NetApp unveil the first fully-managed ONTAP file system in the cloud
summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) and NetApp have launched Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP, the first fully managed ONTAP file system in the cloud. This new service allows customers to run applications on AWS without altering their code or data management, leveraging NetApp's ONTAP technology traditionally used for on-premise network-attached storage (NAS). The collaboration aims to significantly expand digital transformation and AWS adoption, particularly targeting enterprises using NAS for critical applications.

title: One Animation Names New Hires From Hasbro, Amazon
summary: One Animation has announced two new hires to its digital team, bringing in executives from Hasbro and Amazon. Kelly Joeman joins as senior manager of audience development, focusing on amplifying the studio's digital presence and growing its 20 kids-targeted channels. Tuan Nguyen has been appointed e-commerce manager to lead the studio's direct-to-consumer e-commerce business.

title: Amazon FSx for ONTAP for Kubernetes & Containers
summary: This article explores how Amazon FSx for ONTAP enhances Kubernetes and container services within the AWS ecosystem. It details FSx for ONTAP as a fully managed AWS-native service offering advanced file and block storage, addressing persistent storage challenges for containerized workloads. The article examines its integration with Amazon EKS, OpenShift/ROSA, and Amazon ECS, highlighting benefits like unified storage, data portability, and simplified operations.

title: File Sharing with Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP
summary: This article explores the file sharing capabilities of Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP, a collaboration between AWS and NetApp. It highlights how this service simplifies system architectures for multi-region, hybrid, and multicloud deployments by offering multiprotocol file and block storage support, including NFS, SMB, and iSCSI. The piece emphasizes the integration with AWS services and NetApp's data management features, positioning FSx for ONTAP as a comprehensive data platform for digital transformation and cloud migration.

title: How to Set Up Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP with BlueXP Console
summary: This article provides a step-by-step guide on setting up Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP using the NetApp BlueXP Console. It details the process from adding a new working environment and configuring AWS IAM credentials to defining storage capacity, creating a BlueXP Console Connector, and provisioning storage volumes. The guide highlights the benefits of FSx for ONTAP, such as multiprotocol support, high availability, and integration with other AWS services, emphasizing its utility for hybrid and multicloud environments.

title: Stampede for horse med ivermectin, bogus treatment for COVID-19, steers clear of Upper Valley
summary: Despite a national trend of using ivermectin, an animal dewormer, as a false treatment for COVID-19, its misuse is not widespread in the Upper Valley region. Health officials express alarm over online misinformation causing illnesses and an increase in calls to poison control centers nationwide. While local feed stores are starting to lock up ivermectin or add warning signs, some New Hampshire farmers are facing difficulties restocking the drug for their livestock due to demand, highlighting the dangers of using veterinary-grade products on humans.

title: WWD: American Eagle Outfitters Logs $121 Million Profit; Acquires Logistics Company
summary: American Eagle Outfitters reported a $121 million profit and acquired logistics firm Airterra to enhance its supply chain and offer faster delivery services, including same-day delivery. This strategic acquisition positions AEO to compete with major retailers like Amazon, Walmart, and Target in last-mile delivery. The company also saw strong revenue growth across its brands, particularly Aerie, and updated its operating income outlook.

title: Walmart's wage bump signals pressure to raise pay in industry battle for labor
summary: Walmart's decision to raise wages for 565,000 U.S. store workers by at least $1 per hour highlights the intense competition for labor in the retail industry ahead of the crucial holiday shopping season. This move, Walmart's third wage hike in a year, increases its average hourly wage to $16.40 and comes amidst a nationwide worker shortage and the impending end of federal unemployment benefits. While some workers argue the pay is still insufficient, the wage hike reflects growing pressure on retailers to offer more competitive compensation and benefits.

title: JD.com’s Latest $500M Investment Is All About the Warehouse
summary: JD.com's infrastructure management unit has acquired a controlling stake in China Logistics Property Holdings (CNLP) for $513 million, aiming to enhance its fulfillment capabilities across China amidst rising demand and supply chain constraints. This investment will add 65 logistics parks to JD.com's portfolio and could lead to a full takeover of CNLP, reflecting the intensifying competition in China's e-commerce sector and the strategic importance of warehouses and fulfillment centers. The acquisition aligns with JD.com's aggressive logistics investments and its broader ambition for both domestic and international expansion.

title: NetApp ONTAP Storage Platform Available on AWS
summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) has launched Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP, a new fully managed service that allows enterprises to utilize NetApp's ONTAP data management system in the cloud. This service enables users to access all ONTAP capabilities, features, and APIs within an AWS-managed environment, facilitating hybrid cloud strategies and simplifying data migration for on-premises ONTAP users. The offering includes two storage tiers—Primary Storage for active data and Capacity Pool Storage for infrequently accessed data—and supports various access protocols and features.

title: Rivian files for IPO and Goldman Sachs expands automotive portfolio with $110M investment
summary: This article details Rivian's confidential IPO filing, aiming for an $80 billion valuation, and Goldman Sachs's $110 million investment in DealerPolicy, an insurance tech startup. It also covers various other significant investments and acquisitions in the automotive technology space, including deals in EV battery lifecycle management, automotive cybersecurity, and autonomous driving. The piece highlights a busy M&A environment driven by substantial undeployed private equity and venture capital.

title: Amazon to open 200,000-square-foot delivery station on Northern Virginia's outskirts
summary: Amazon.com Inc. is set to open a new 200,000-square-foot delivery station in Fredericksburg, Virginia, later this month. This move is part of the e-commerce giant's strategy to locate larger fulfillment centers just outside major metropolitan areas.

title: Thinking outside the box: AWS signals a new era for storage
summary: Amazon Web Services is projected to generate $9 billion in storage revenue in 2021, becoming the second-largest enterprise storage supplier behind Dell Technologies, and is expected to surpass $11 billion in 2022. At its third annual Storage Day, AWS announced a significant partnership with NetApp Inc. to run its full ONTAP stack natively in the cloud as a managed service, alongside other storage service enhancements. This move signals AWS's continued drive to innovate in data storage, challenging traditional on-premises models and expanding into hybrid cloud and data mesh conversations.

title: EXCLUSIVE Amazon considers more proactive approach to determining what belongs on its cloud service
summary: Amazon is reportedly planning to adopt a more proactive strategy to identify and remove content on its Amazon Web Services (AWS) cloud platform that violates its policies, such as those against promoting violence. This initiative involves expanding the Trust & Safety team and hiring specialists to monitor for emerging threats. While an AWS spokesperson initially denied changes and stated the existing team already handles abusive content, the move suggests a potential shift towards greater content arbitration by the leading cloud provider, raising free speech debates.

title: Alphabet, Tesla and Amazon are among the most favourite stocks held by US-focused mutual funds. Here are top 10 stocks
summary: This article identifies Alphabet, Tesla, and Amazon as top stock holdings among U.S.-focused mutual funds available to Indian investors. It details 10 such mutual funds, highlighting their investment strategies, underlying assets, and historical performance. The funds provide Indian investors exposure to leading US companies and geographical diversification.

title: Kroger eyes potential entry into Southwest Florida marketplace
summary: Kroger is planning to expand its online-only grocery delivery service into Southwest Florida, eyeing Naples and Fort Myers for a new distribution "spoke" facility within the next year. This expansion would create up to 180 new jobs and intensify competition with existing grocery delivery services from Publix, Walmart, Target, and Amazon, all without building any physical stores. Kroger's strategy relies on highly automated fulfillment centers and "spoke" facilities to extend delivery reach.

title: Lennox announces new integration of its iComfort thermostat
summary: Lennox has expanded the compatibility of its iComfort thermostats to integrate with various smart home automation platforms, including premium systems like Control4 and popular virtual assistants such as Amazon Alexa, Apple HomeKit, Google Assistant, and IFTTT. This integration allows users to manage their Lennox heating and cooling systems through a wider range of smart home devices, offering enhanced convenience and control over their indoor environment. Control4 customers with Lennox HVAC systems and iComfort S30, E30, or M30 thermostats can request integration through their dealer, enabling centralized control from their smart home system.

title: PayPal Buys Paidy in A $2.7 Billion Deal to Expand Buy Now Pay Later Service
summary: PayPal Holdings Inc. announced its acquisition of Japanese buy now, pay later (BNPL) firm Paidy for 300 billion yen ($2.7 billion) to expand its presence in Japan, the world's third-largest e-commerce market. This cash deal, expected to close in Q4 2021, aims to leverage Paidy's established BNPL solutions and 6 million users to boost PayPal's position in this strategically important market. The acquisition is part of a larger trend in the payment industry, with other major players like Square and Amazon also investing heavily in BNPL services.

title: Kroger says it's not trying to steal business from Publix with delivery service
summary: Kroger CEO Rodney McMullen stated the company is not trying to take market share from Publix in Florida despite launching grocery delivery services in Tampa and Jacksonville, with Miami next. Kroger's strategy leverages its new high-tech distribution center in Groveland to provide seamless e-commerce service, recognizing high brand familiarity among Floridians and the shift in post-pandemic shopping habits. The company plans to expand slowly based on customer experience, with no current plans for physical stores in the state.

title: DC reveals details on first WEBTOON series, a FaZe Clan comic collaboration, and more for Batman Day
summary: DC has announced a host of events and releases for Batman Day on September 18th, including the debut of "Batman: Wayne Family Adventures," its first Webtoon original series. The celebrations also feature a collaboration with eSports organization FaZe Clan for an exclusive comic and the release of the scripted podcast "Batman: The Audio Adventures" on HBO Max. Additionally, DC is launching "Batman: The World," a global hardcover anthology, and offering various other comic, toy, and multimedia experiences for fans.

title: Amazon EKS Anywhere launches into general availability
summary: Amazon Web Services Inc. has announced the general availability of Amazon EKS Anywhere, an extension of its Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service. This new service allows customers to run Kubernetes clusters on-premises using VMware vSphere, providing an installable software package and automation tools for cluster lifecycle support. EKS Anywhere, similar to Google's Anthos and Microsoft's Azure Arc, is intended to simplify Kubernetes management across both cloud and on-premises environments, addressing the need for consistent management and deployment mechanisms for hybrid cloud operations.

title: Semiconductors to account for 20% of vehicle cost by 2030
summary: New research from Intel Corp. forecasts that semiconductors will constitute over 20% of the total premium vehicle bill of materials by 2030, a fivefold increase from 2019. This growth is driven by the increasing demand for semiconductors in various digital markets, including automotive, and Intel is expanding its manufacturing efforts with significant investments in new fabs to meet this demand. The company is also working to transition automotive chips to more advanced process technologies.

title: Macy’s Sales Plummeted in 2020, Highlighting Pandemic’s Toll on Retail (Published 2021)
summary: Macy's sales plunged 29% in 2020 to $17.3 billion, resulting in a net loss of $3.9 billion, largely due to the pandemic's impact on retail. The company is focusing on expanding its digital business, moving out of traditional malls, and testing smaller store formats to adapt to shifting consumer preferences. Macy's CEO Jeff Gennette noted the significant decline in apparel sales, particularly "dressy" clothing, and anticipates a recovery in the latter half of 2021.

title: Prevent Container Risks With Advanced Container Image Sandboxing
summary: Palo Alto Networks announced new capabilities in Prisma Cloud's Cloud Workload Protection to enhance container security, particularly through advanced machine learning for pre-deployment image sandboxing. This allows developers and DevOps teams to analyze third-party container images for dynamic threats in an isolated environment before deployment. The update also expands host security for VMs on Azure and Google Cloud, improves web application and API security, and includes Red Hat certification for its vulnerability scanner.

title: Amazon to open warehouse in Delta Township, bringing 500 jobs
summary: Amazon.com, Inc. announced plans to open a 1-million-square-foot fulfillment center in Delta Township, Michigan, which will create over 500 full-time jobs. This will be Amazon's eighth fulfillment center in the state and its first in mid-Michigan, focusing on larger items. The facility is expected to be operational next year, with employees earning an average of $17 an hour plus healthcare benefits.

title: Ulta Beauty Inc. stock outperforms competitors on strong trading day
summary: Ulta Beauty Inc. (ULTA) stock rose 1.54% to $382.08 on a generally down day for the market, outperforming the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average. The stock closed $32.90 below its 52-week high and also outperformed key competitors like CVS Health Corp., Walgreens Boots Alliance Inc., and Amazon.com Inc. Trading volume was slightly below its 50-day average.

title: Will Snowflake Be Worth More Than Salesforce.com by 2030?
summary: This article analyzes whether Snowflake could surpass Salesforce.com in market capitalization by 2030, comparing their growth rates and valuations. While Snowflake projects rapid revenue growth, its current high valuation makes it unlikely to maintain its price-to-sales ratio for a decade, suggesting Salesforce will remain more valuable. However, Snowflake's stock could still offer bigger gains due to its aggressive growth targets, despite facing more competition.

title: Find Lost Items at Home with Alexa, Google, Xfinity, and Siri
summary: This article provides guidance on how to locate lost items within a home using various smart assistants such as Alexa, Google, Xfinity, and Siri. It covers different methods and tips for leveraging these technologies to find misplaced belongings.

title: Alibaba-Backed Hello Inc. to Complete New Round of Financing
summary: Alibaba-Backed Hello Inc. is preparing to complete a new round of financing. This development indicates ongoing investment and growth for the company, which operates in a sector of interest for major tech players like Alibaba.

title: Protect Your Data with Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP
summary: This article discusses how Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP helps solve complex data protection challenges in hybrid and multicloud environments. It details features like Snapshots, block-level backups, disaster recovery, and data governance with Cloud Data Sense. These capabilities enable cost-effective data management, enhanced security, and compliance with regulatory requirements.

title: Tennessee panel OKs $65M in state incentives for Oracle
summary: A Tennessee panel has approved $65 million in state incentives for Oracle Corp. The company plans to create 8,500 jobs and invest $1.2 billion in Nashville over the next decade, with an average salary of $110,000. This expansion would surpass Amazon's previous investment in the city.

title: UPS to hire over 100k essential seasonal workers
summary: UPS announced its plan to hire over 100,000 essential seasonal workers to manage the anticipated increase in package volume during the 2021 holiday season, which runs from October 2021 through January 2022. The company aims for a quick hiring process, with many qualified candidates receiving an offer within 30 minutes of applying. UPS also highlighted its track record of converting seasonal roles into permanent positions, with nearly a third of its current U.S. workforce having started in seasonal jobs.

title: Apple can’t force developers to use its in-app payment system, federal judge rules
summary: A federal judge ruled that Apple Inc. can no longer compel developers to use its in-app payment system, allowing them to bypass commission fees of 15% to 30%. This decision, stemming from the Epic Games Inc. case, could significantly alter how apps are distributed by dominant online platforms like Apple, Alphabet Inc. (Google), and Amazon.com Inc. However, the ruling stopped short of declaring Apple an antitrust monopolist.

title: How Dutch grocery giant Ahold Delhaize is taking on U.S. rivals with tech
summary: Ahold Delhaize, a Dutch grocery conglomerate, is leveraging technology and strategic acquisitions to compete with major U.S. rivals like Kroger, Walmart, and Albertsons, especially in the online grocery market. The company, which operates brands like Stop & Shop and Food Lion in the U.S., is investing in automated distribution centers, launching new e-commerce platforms like Ship2Me, and focusing on organic growth and smaller urban stores. CEO Frans Muller believes hybrid fulfillment models and catering to changed consumer habits post-pandemic, such as increased home cooking, will sustain their growth.

title: “We are not giving up.” Alabama Coal Miners Enter Sixth Month of Strike
summary: Alabama coal miners at Warrior Met Coal Inc. have entered their sixth month of a historic strike, fighting for better wages, reasonable hours, and improved safety conditions against a company that declared bankruptcy and then exploited its workers. The article details the harsh working conditions, the workers' personal sacrifices, and the political complexities and contradictions encountered during the prolonged labor dispute, highlighting the efforts by the Left Voice to support and amplify their message. Despite challenges and limited support from mainstream media and politicians, the miners remain determined, with solidarity efforts extending to other labor movements, including efforts by a Women's Auxiliary Committee.

title: Naturally Network to Launch Officially at Expo East
summary: Naturally Network, a new national trade association for the natural and organic product industry, will officially launch at Natural Products Expo East. Founded in June, the 501(c)(6) business association aims to foster growth and support local affiliates, members, and sponsors across the country. Executive Director Sharon Reddehase will lead the organization, which has already established a board of directors and secured founding sponsors through its Founders Circle.

title: Single Stocks & ETFs Do Mix
summary: This article discusses how single stocks and ETFs can both have a place in an investment portfolio. It highlights the similarities and differences, emphasizing the importance of considering overall portfolio concentration when adding individual stocks. The author also weighs the pros and cons, such as lower costs for single stocks versus the diversification and professional management benefits of ETFs.

title: Apple, Google, Amazon spying on you, lawsuits claim
summary: Lawsuits allege that Apple, Google, and Amazon are spying on users through their voice assistants, recording private conversations and sharing them with advertisers. A class-action lawsuit against Apple's Siri has been greenlit by a federal judge, with similar claims made against Google and Amazon. The companies deny these allegations, stating that recordings are only kept with user consent or to improve service, and offer options for users to manage their privacy settings.

title: Copado raises $140 million on $1.2B valuation to expand its DevOps platform
summary: Copado, a DevOps platform for Salesforce, has secured $140 million in Series C funding, led by Insight Partners, pushing its valuation to nearly $1.2 billion. The company plans to use the new capital to expand its DevOps and AI-driven testing solutions across various enterprise SaaS platforms and accelerate international growth, especially in the Asia-Pacific region. Copado, founded in 2013, initially focused on Salesforce but has since expanded to support other cloud platforms and has acquired DevSecOps and AI-testing companies.

title: GetYourGuide gets help from Expedia, Amazon widens virtual tours
summary: Expedia has partnered with GetYourGuide to distribute tours and activities, allowing customers to book GetYourGuide's offerings directly on Expedia's sites. This move follows Expedia's shift to sourcing third-party inventory after closing its own concierge business. Simultaneously, Amazon has expanded its virtual tours service, Amazon Explore, to include small group experiences, enabling multiple customers from different locations to participate in live virtual activities.

title: Cloudflare Workers: the Fast Serverless Platform
summary: This article discusses Cloudflare Workers, a serverless platform designed for speed and efficiency at the edge. It highlights how Workers significantly outperform other serverless offerings like Lambda and Lambda@Edge in terms of speed and addresses the challenges posed by traditional container-based serverless architectures by leveraging lightweight V8 isolates. The post emphasizes that Workers' architecture eliminates cold starts and provides a better developer and end-user experience due to its global edge network and continuous performance improvements.

title: Redesigned Sonos Beam supports Dolby Atmos, eARC
summary: Sonos has redesigned its Beam soundbar, now in its second generation, to include Dolby Atmos support and HDMI eARC connectivity. The newer model retains the compact size of its predecessor but features a faster CPU for virtualized Dolby Atmos height effects and an updated polycarbonate grille. Shipping October 5 for $449, it will also support lossless and Dolby Atmos Music from Amazon Music.

title: Kroger and Instacart launch 30-minute grocery delivery service in the U.S.
summary: Kroger and Instacart have partnered to launch "Kroger Delivery Now," a new home-delivery service promising groceries and household staples in as little as 30 minutes. This offering aims to reach up to 50 million U.S. households, significantly expanding Kroger's e-commerce presence amid competition from Walmart and Amazon. The service emphasizes convenience, providing quick delivery of 25,000 items through Kroger's platforms and a dedicated "Convenience Hub" on Instacart.

summary: This page provides a comprehensive overview of Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste (ASR) stock, including its current price, key data points, return performance against the S&P, company information, and recent news and analysis. It also presents detailed financial health metrics, valuation ratios, and earnings call transcripts for investors.

title: Spotify Rival Anghami partners with Amazon to give Prime members in Saudi Arabia and UAE 6 months Anghami Plus for free
summary: Anghami, a music streaming company focused on the Middle East and North Africa, has teamed up with Amazon to provide Prime members in Saudi Arabia and the UAE with a free six-month subscription to its premium service, Anghami Plus. This collaboration will be followed by a 50% discount for the subsequent six months. The partnership aims to offer Prime members access to millions of songs, podcasts, and unlimited downloads, enhancing their entertainment benefits in regions where Amazon Music Unlimited is not currently available.

title: Intuit (INTU) to Buy Digital Marketing Firm Mailchimp for $12B
summary: Intuit (INTU) announced its agreement to acquire digital marketing firm Mailchimp for $12 billion in a cash-and-stock deal, expected to close by the end of fiscal second-quarter 2022. This acquisition aims to boost Intuit's small-business capabilities and enhance its customer reach by integrating Mailchimp’s email marketing services and AI-driven technology with Intuit’s QuickBooks platform. The deal is intended to provide an end-to-end customer growth platform for small and mid-market businesses and is anticipated to be accretive to Intuit’s fiscal 2022 adjusted earnings.

title: The Sonos Beam Gen 2 Is Now Available | WiFiHiFi
summary: The Sonos Beam Gen 2 is a new compact soundbar with enhanced processing power, supporting Dolby Atmos and Ultra HD audio. Available for pre-order at $559 in Canada, it features a faster CPU, re-tuned speaker arrays for crisper dialogue, and eARC compatibility for a more immersive sound experience. Sonos also plans to support Amazon Music's Ultra High Definition audio and Dolby Atmos Music on various Sonos speakers, while the Beam Gen 2 introduces a new polycarbonate grille and NFC for easier setup.

title: Amazon hikes average U.S. starting pay to $18, hires for 125,000 jobs
summary: Amazon has increased its average U.S. starting wage to over $18 an hour and plans to hire an additional 125,000 warehouse and transportation workers. This move comes amidst a tight U.S. labor market and increased scrutiny of Amazon's labor practices. The company aims to fill these roles quickly to support its continued growth and enhance its logistics capabilities, including its one-day delivery service for Prime members.

title: Procore Appoints Sandra Benson as Global Head of Industry Transformation
summary: Procore Technologies, Inc. has appointed construction technology expert Sandra Benson as its Global Head of Industry Transformation. In this new role, Benson will advise Procore’s product and sales engineering teams on customer and partner requirements, leveraging her extensive experience in the building and construction technology industry. She is also a presidential appointee to the Board of Directors of the National Institute of Building Sciences (NIBS).

title: SAP and Amazon Business Partner to Expand Buyer Choice
summary: SAP and Amazon Business have partnered to integrate Amazon Business into SAP Ariba solutions, allowing employees to purchase from Amazon Business directly within SAP Ariba. This collaboration aims to expand buyer choice and simplify procurement for general business goods, leveraging a real-time search API and extending to the Concur Expense solution. The integration is set to roll out globally, beginning with early adopters in the United States.

title: After Brazil, Shopee tops rankings in Mexico, Colombia and Chile - now available to 1B people
summary: Shopee has expanded its dominance in Latin America, becoming the most downloaded shopping app in Mexico, Colombia, and Chile, mirroring its success in Brazil. Parent company Sea Ltd. secured an additional US$6 billion in funding to fuel aggressive market expansion. Shopee is also planning to enter the European market, starting with Poland, seeking to replicate its developing-world success in more established economies.

title: Real Estate Roundup: North Phoenix office building sells for $22M and 10 other deals to know
summary: This article provides a roundup of recent real estate transactions and store openings in the Valley area. It highlights the sale of a North Phoenix office building for $22 million, an apartment sale in Tempe, a surgery center sale in Chandler, and a land sale in Surprise. The report covers nearly a dozen significant real estate deals and new establishments across the region.

title: Kendall Jenner Was Influenced By Instagram To Buy Her Camo Crocs
summary: Kendall Jenner appeared on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon and revealed that she bought her "controversial" camo Crocs due to Instagram influencing her. She saw them on a fashion inspiration page and found them "too cute." This comes as Crocs sees a surge in popularity and anticipates doubling its revenue to over $5 billion by 2026.

title: Need A Job? Amazon Hiring Thousands Of Employees Including Michig
summary: Amazon is looking to hire 125,000 employees across the country, including in Michigan, with pay ranging from $18 to $22.50 per hour. The company offers comprehensive benefits, including health, vision, and dental insurance, 401(k) with company match, paid parental leave, and full college tuition for front-line employees through its Career Choice program. Interested applicants can find open positions and apply at hiring.amazon.com.

title: Calavo Growers appoints Amazon executive as CFO
summary: Calavo Growers, Inc. announced the appointment of Mariela Matute as Chief Financial Officer, effective October 11, 2021. Matute previously served as Director and CFO for Amazon Business, bringing extensive financial expertise and relevant industry background to Calavo. The company expects her leadership to help execute its strategic plan, accelerate profitable growth, and enhance shareholder value.

title: Carvana CEO’s dad goes on $3.6B stock selling spree, raising eyebrows
summary: Carvana CEO's father, Ernie Garcia II, has sold over $3.6 billion in company stock since October, raising concerns about the family's control over the used car dealership. This selling spree, facilitated by a predetermined plan that was modified twice, follows a period where Garcia II and his son bought shares at "bargain basement" prices during the pandemic, leading to a lawsuit for insider trading. Despite the massive sales, Garcia II still holds a significant stake, with the company's annual report even warning that the Garcia family's interests might not always align with other stockholders.

title: Corsair Sabre RGB Pro Wireless gaming mouse review
summary: The Corsair Sabre RGB Pro Wireless gaming mouse offers an ultra-light build, strong performance, and freedom of movement, despite being slightly less fast than its wired counterpart. It features 2K polling, 26K DPI, and customizable settings through the robust iCue software, making it an affordable and versatile option for most gamers.

title: Highly Immersive Phygital Malls
summary: JD.com has launched a massive 42,000-square-meter "phygital" shopping mall in Xi'an, China, aiming to blend physical and digital retail experiences. The mall features five floors with over 200,000 items from 150 brands, allowing shoppers to scan QR codes for home delivery. It also incorporates interactive technology like holographic projections, VR equipment, and AI robots to enhance the immersive experience.

title: Salesforce values and culture driven innovation
summary: This article explores how Salesforce has evolved from a CRM company to a leading cloud and productivity organization, driven by its core values and culture. Field CTO Adam Spearing discusses how the company's focus has shifted towards digital transformation, accelerated by the pandemic, and highlights key acquisitions like Tableau and Slack. The piece emphasizes the importance of culture, customer-centric innovation, and collaborative ecosystems in Salesforce's strategy for future growth.

title: WSJ News Exclusive | CEO’s Father Gets a $3.6 Billion Stock Windfall at Carvana
summary: Ernie Garcia II, father of Carvana Co.'s CEO, has sold over $3.6 billion in Carvana stock since October, representing 16% of his holdings. This windfall is attributed to a corporate ownership structure that benefits the family and allows them to maintain control, though it may be at the expense of other shareholders. The article highlights how his stock sales rank him among the top individuals for earnings from company stock sales in the past year, excluding prominent tech and retail magnates.

title: Is a stock market correction on the horizon?
summary: The S&P 500 has seen a recent dip, leading analysts to narrow predictions for the U.S. equity market. While tech stocks may face challenges due to Fed policy and rising interest rates, other sectors like energy and small-caps are showing potential. Despite concerns, corrections are normal, and many analysts remain bullish on long-term market growth, suggesting current dips could be buying opportunities.

title: 39 Billion by 2026: America’s Carriers Will Nearly Double Their Package Hauls, Data Shows
summary: A Pitney Bowes report indicates U.S. parcel volume surged 37% in 2020 to 20 billion, driven by e-commerce due to the pandemic. The study forecasts a near doubling of parcel volume to 32-39 billion by 2026, with a 10% CAGR. Major carriers like UPS, FedEx, and USPS saw significant revenue growth, while Amazon Logistics rapidly increased its market share.

title: How GoodRx Fended Off Amazon
summary: GoodRx, a prescription drug comparison app, has successfully thrived despite competition from Amazon's prescription drug discount program. The company has seen significant growth in revenue and customer numbers, driven by a rebound in prescription volumes and strategic diversification into telehealth and other health technology solutions. GoodRx plans further expansion into complementary markets to address various consumer pain points in healthcare.

title: The Climate Pledge announces 86 new signatories
summary: The Climate Pledge, co-founded by Amazon and Global Optimism, has announced 86 new signatories, bringing the total to over 201 companies committed to achieving net-zero carbon by 2040, ten years ahead of the Paris Agreement. These new additions, including major businesses like Nespresso, ASOS, Procter & Gamble, HP, and Salesforce, represent various industries across 21 countries and are collectively expected to significantly mitigate carbon emissions. The initiative emphasizes collaboration and real business changes in response to the urgent climate crisis highlighted by recent IPCC reports.

title: Mattel, Warner Music Group's Arts Music Release He-Man, Hot Wheels, Thomas & Friends Albums
summary: Mattel has partnered with Warner Music Group's Arts Music division to release new albums based on popular franchises like He-Man and the Masters of the Universe, Hot Wheels, and Thomas & Friends. These releases build upon an existing multi-year global music licensing agreement. The new albums feature original soundtracks and theme songs from their respective series, with additional releases planned for the future across major digital music platforms.

title: Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP – The easiest storage decision you’ll ever make
summary: This article argues that Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP is the easiest storage decision for businesses, highlighting its simplicity, built-in technology, and security. The author contrasts FSx for ONTAP's quick setup and transparent pricing with the complexity, high costs, and longer commitment periods associated with Dell's Cloud Storage Services and Pure Storage's Cloud Block Store. The piece emphasizes FSx for ONTAP's native AWS integration and comprehensive features, positioning it as a superior and more cost-effective solution for hybrid cloud storage.

title: The Climate Pledge Announces 86 New Signatories, Including Procter & Gamble, HP, and Salesforce, Signaling Their Commitment to Achieving Net-Zero Carbon by 2040 or Sooner.
summary: The Climate Pledge has announced 86 new signatories, including major companies like Procter & Gamble, HP, and Salesforce, bringing the total to over 200 global organizations. These companies commit to achieving net-zero carbon by 2040, a decade ahead of the Paris Agreement, and are collectively expected to mitigate 1.98 billion metric tons of carbon emissions annually by 2040. The announcement emphasizes the urgency of collective action by businesses to address climate change based on recent IPCC findings.

title: Lionsgate A Juicy M&A Target, Vice Chair Michael Burns Agrees
summary: Lionsgate Vice Chairman Michael Burns acknowledged the company is a prime M&A target amid media industry consolidation, stating that its goal is to increase stock value. He highlighted Lionsgate's nimbleness and extensive library as key advantages, especially in the streaming era. Burns also commented on the evolving landscape of talent deals and theatrical windows, describing it as the "Wild West."

title: Lionsgate Vice Chair: “There’s Great Scarcity Value” in Being a Major Indie Studio Now
summary: Lionsgate vice chairman Michael Burns believes the Hollywood studio is an attractive takeover target due to its status as a large independent company amidst ongoing industry consolidation and the streaming boom. He highlights the "scarcity value" of independent studios and Lionsgate's strategy of acquiring content libraries while others focus on mergers. Burns also discussed the evolving landscape of talent compensation as films increasingly move directly to streaming.

title: Rackspace Launches Rackspace Data Freedom to Eliminate Cloud Lock-In
summary: Rackspace Technology has introduced Rackspace Data Freedom, a new platform designed to help organizations avoid cloud lock-in by separating storage from public cloud compute. This service aims to eliminate unpredictable data egress charges, allowing customers to save on costs and maintain data sovereignty across multi-cloud environments. Key benefits include significant cost reduction through Rackspace's private network, enhanced data accessibility via RackConnect Global, and customized storage solutions to meet specific user requirements.

title: Kilroy Pays $490M for Amazon-Anchored Tower
summary: Kilroy Realty Corp. acquired West 8th, a 539,000-square-foot, LEED Platinum certified office tower in Seattle, for $490 million. The building is fully leased, with Amazon occupying approximately 70 percent of the space, and was previously purchased by DWS Group in 2016 for $370 million. This acquisition expands Kilroy's Seattle footprint and follows other significant investments and a disposition by the REIT in Texas and San Francisco.

title: BSX Begins Publishing MIAX Pearl Equities
summary: The Bermuda Stock Exchange (BSX), a subsidiary of Miami International Holdings, Inc., has started publishing MIAX Pearl Equities market data for 10 actively traded U.S. companies to the Pyth Network. This marks BSX's first initiative to provide high-fidelity data to the Pyth Network, contributing U.S. equities exchange market data to support DeFi markets. The initial companies include Apple, Amazon, Google, Netflix, and Tesla.

title: FedEx labor shortfall hits quarterly profit, earnings forecast
summary: FedEx (FDX.N) reported a 7% drop in quarterly profit and lowered its full-year earnings forecast due to labor shortages, which led to increased costs and slowed package delivery. The company incurred an extra $450 million in costs from higher wages, overtime, and third-party transportation, particularly affecting its Ground network which is now rerouting 600,000 packages daily. FedEx plans to hire 90,000 holiday workers to address staffing issues as it prepares for the peak season.

title: BSX publishes market data to Pyth Network
summary: The Bermuda Stock Exchange (BSX) has started publishing MIAX Pearl Equities market data for ten US companies to the Pyth Network, a decentralized financial market data distribution platform. This initiative marks BSX's first step in providing high-fidelity data to the blockchain industry via the Solana network, with plans to expand the data breadth. The included companies are major US firms like Apple, Amazon, and Tesla, marking a significant development for DeFi markets.

title: Netflix Inc. stock outperforms competitors on strong trading day
summary: Shares of Netflix Inc. (NFLX) rose 3.06% to $590.65 on Wednesday, outperforming the S&P 500 Index and Dow Jones Industrial Average. The stock's performance also beat out some competitors like Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) and Walt Disney Co. (DIS), although Comcast Corp. Cl A (CMCSA) saw a slight dip. This rise snapped a two-day losing streak for Netflix.

title: Brian Roberts: Comcast is ‘Really a Broadband Company’
summary: Comcast chairman/CEO Brian Roberts stated that Comcast has transformed into a broadband company, having accumulated 33 million customers and adding about 1 million broadband subscribers annually for two decades. This growth greatly offsets declines in cable TV subscriptions. Roberts emphasized the company's focus on deepening broadband relationships through enhanced connectivity and new devices like XiOne, positioning Comcast as a leader in the evolving high-speed Internet landscape.

title: The Market Remains Hot As We Kick Off Our Next Forrester Wave™ Evaluation Of The DAM Landscape
summary: Forrester is launching its next Wave evaluation for Digital Asset Management (DAM) due to significant market growth and increasing customer demand. Many organizations struggle with content creation challenges, such as outdated processes, content volume outpacing production capabilities, and the need for better personalization foundations. DAM solutions offer governance, centralization, metadata enrichment, content atomization, and AI-powered tagging, distinguishing them from basic cloud storage options.

title: General Motors and Amazon Team Up to Offer OnStar Emergency Service at Home
summary: General Motors and Amazon have partnered to introduce the OnStar Guardian skill for Amazon Alexa, enabling users to access OnStar's Emergency-Certified Advisors at home through Alexa-enabled devices. This new feature allows family members to call for help in various crisis situations, extending OnStar's safety and security services beyond the vehicle to in-home environments. The service will initially roll out to select OnStar members, with a broader release planned for 2022.

title: Kilroy Realty buys Amazon-leased tower in Seattle's Denny Triangle for $490M
summary: Kilroy Realty, a Los Angeles-based real estate firm, has acquired an Amazon-leased tower in Seattle's Denny Triangle for $490 million. This acquisition signals Kilroy Realty's confidence in major tenants eventually returning to physical offices, despite the ongoing uncertainty surrounding office reopening plans. The purchase highlights the continued investment interest in Seattle's commercial real estate market, especially for properties anchored by large tech companies.

title: Iconix Brand Group Steps Into The Footwear Market With New Licensee for Starter
summary: Iconix Brand Group has signed a three-year licensing agreement with Genesco Inc. to make them the exclusive US and Canadian footwear licensee for STARTER. This deal marks Starter’s return to footwear in the U.S. and Canada after a five-year absence, with a collection of approximately 30 SKUs planned to launch in Spring 2022. The partnership aims to capitalize on the growing consumer demand for heritage brands and expand STARTER's presence in the athletic footwear market.

title: Cisco Named a Leader in 2021 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for WAN Edge Infrastructure
summary: Cisco has announced its recognition as a Leader in the 2021 Gartner Magic Quadrant for WAN Edge Infrastructure, highlighting its SD-WAN solutions. These solutions focus on enabling secure, predictable digital experiences for hybrid workforces, building dynamic workspaces, and securing multi-cloud environments, accelerating the transition to a SASE-enabled architecture. Cisco emphasizes its comprehensive capabilities in seamless multicloud access, integrated security, and optimized insights through ThousandEyes integration.

title: Autonomous pilot program tests Paccar-built FedEx trucks in Texas
summary: A new pilot program is testing autonomous Paccar-built FedEx trucks in Texas, utilizing self-driving technology from an Amazon-backed startup. These trucks will operate with a safety driver, autonomously hauling FedEx loads on a 500-mile round trip between Dallas and Houston. The initiative highlights ongoing advancements and investments in autonomous vehicle technology for commercial logistics.

title: Amazon's cloud unit to create data centres, 1,000 jobs in New Zealand
summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) announced plans to launch data centres in New Zealand by 2024, investing NZ$7.5 billion ($5.25 billion) in a new infrastructure hub. This initiative is expected to create approximately 1,000 jobs in the country over 15 years. The new hub will allow developers, startups, and government entities to use local data centres, fostering digital transformation and economic growth.

title: Samsung to make Tesla’s HW 4.0 self-driving auto chip
summary: Samsung Electronics Co. has won the contract to manufacture Tesla Inc.'s next-generation hardware 4 (HW 4.0) chip for its autonomous driving technology, beating out TSMC. Samsung plans to mass-produce the HW 4.0 chip using 7-nanometer processing technology, ensuring higher production yields and stable functions for Tesla's upcoming vehicles like the Cybertruck. This partnership strengthens Samsung's position in the global foundry market as it competes with TSMC and expands its collaborations with other tech giants like Google and Amazon.

title: If You Missed the PS5 Restock, Here’s How to Prepare for the Next One
summary: This article discusses the ongoing PS5 stock shortages, nearly a year after its release, exacerbated by the pandemic and chip shortages. It offers tips for securing a console during future restocks, such as signing up for retailer accounts with current billing/shipping info, avoiding PayPal for faster checkout, and following Twitter alert accounts like @PS5StockAlerts, @mattswider, and @Wario64. The piece highlights that despite recent rumors of a major restock, consoles quickly sold out.

title: Barclays announces new CEO of point-of-sale finance business
summary: Barclays has appointed Antony Stephen as the new CEO of its point-of-sale finance business, Barclays Partner Finance, effective October 4, 2021. Stephen, who previously served as Head of Amazon Payments Europe, will focus on expanding the UK point-of-sale finance business and providing leadership for Barclays Cubed, the bank's next-generation commerce platform. His extensive experience in payments and financial services is expected to drive growth and innovation in the rapidly evolving point-of-sale finance market.

title: Daxko
summary: Daxko, a SaaS platform for fitness center management, faced significant challenges during the COVID-19 pandemic due to its customers being heavily impacted. To manage rapid changes, integrate nine acquisitions, and provide crucial support to its clients, Daxko implemented IBM Instana Observability. This allowed them to quickly adapt their product roadmap, gain comprehensive visibility into their complex IT environment, and minimize downtime, ultimately helping their customers navigate the unprecedented times.

title: Starbucks pushes back against US workers’ cafe-by-cafe union vote
authors: ['Amelia Pollard and Josh Eidelson and Bloomberg']
summary: Starbucks is opposing unionization efforts by workers in Buffalo, New York, arguing that any union vote should encompass all 20 of its Buffalo-area locations rather than individual cafes. The company's stance challenges a labor board precedent that typically favors smaller bargaining units, with a hearing officer noting that single-location units are "presumptively appropriate." This move by Starbucks aligns with employer preferences for larger units to make unionization more difficult, amidst a broader wave of labor activism at nonunion companies.

title: Viral TikTok video accuses Zillow and others of manipulating the housing market. Here’s what’s really going on
summary: A viral TikTok video by Nevada real-estate agent Sean Gotcher claims that companies like Zillow and Redfin are manipulating home prices through their "iBuying" business model. However, real-estate experts suggest the situation is more complex, and a professor noted that if the residential housing market could be rigged so easily, realtors would have done so long ago. The core of the accusation is that a company uses search data to strategically purchase homes in specific ZIP codes.

title: Avantis U.S. Large Cap Value ETF
summary: The Avantis U.S. Large Cap Value ETF (AVLV) offers investors exposure to large-cap U.S. value equities with an active management strategy. The ETF has an expense ratio of 0.15% and has shown strong performance across various timeframes compared to its category average. It holds a diversified portfolio with significant allocations to finance, retail trade, and electronic technology sectors, and its top holdings include major tech and industrial companies.

title: Intel breaks ground on $20 bln Arizona plants as U.S. chip factory race heats up
summary: Intel has broken ground on two new $20 billion chip factories in Arizona, named Fab 52 and Fab 62, as part of its strategy to regain leadership in advanced chip manufacturing and become a major producer for external customers. These plants will be crucial for Intel's goal to lead in chip technology by 2025 and will bolster the U.S. chip supply chain. CEO Pat Gelsinger noted the facilities will also serve outside companies like Qualcomm and Amazon, and Intel plans a new U.S. campus with additional factories by year-end.

title: Astera Labs, a fabless chip startup, nabs $50M at a $950M valuation to remove bottlenecks in high-bandwidth cloud applications
summary: Astera Labs, a fabless semiconductor company, has raised $50 million in a Series C funding round, valuing the company at $950 million post-money. This funding, led by Fidelity Management and Research, will help the company scale operations and launch new product lines to address bottlenecks in high-bandwidth cloud applications, especially for AI and machine learning workloads. Intel, a strategic backer and customer, is collaborating with Astera Labs on developing PCI Express and CXL technology to enhance server and storage infrastructure.

title: Is eBay (EBAY) Stock a Good Buy?
summary: This article evaluates eBay (EBAY) as a potential stock investment, detailing its history, market presence, and financial performance. It highlights eBay's pioneering role in e-commerce, its current standing with 182 million buyers, and significant returns on historical investment, while also discussing the ongoing competition with online retail giants like Amazon. The piece offers guidance on purchasing eBay stock and considers its future outlook given marketplace investments and competitive pressures.

title: Intel’s $20B Project Moves Forward
summary: Intel has broken ground on two new chip factories, Fab 52 and Fab 62, at its Ocotillo campus in Chandler, Arizona, representing a $20 billion investment. This expansion will significantly increase Intel's production capacity, create thousands of tech and construction jobs, and is part of a broader strategy to enhance its chip manufacturing capabilities and compete with other major chipmakers. The project also highlights Intel's long-term commitment to Arizona and its focus on sustainability and benefiting from favorable U.S. legislation promoting domestic semiconductor production.

title: CareBand and Life360 tap Amazon technology to help people stay connected
summary: CareBand and Life360 are partnering with Amazon to utilize Amazon Sidewalk, a shared community network, to enhance the connectivity and reliability of their devices. CareBand's wearable devices will help people with dementia stay safe and connected by extending tracking capabilities beyond their homes. Life360 is integrating Sidewalk with its Jiobit Smart Tags to provide improved location tracking for families, children, elderly parents, and pets, ultimately offering greater peace of mind.

title: Tommy Hilfiger to launch Higg Index Sustainability Profiles
summary: Tommy Hilfiger, owned by PVH Corp, is launching Higg Index Sustainability Profiles for a selection of its products in a pilot program with Amazon, the Sustainable Apparel Coalition (SAC), and Higg. This initiative aims to provide customers with data-backed environmental claims and increased transparency regarding product impact. The pilot will run for six weeks on Tommy Hilfiger's EU e-commerce sites and include items in Amazon's Climate Pledge Friendly program.

title: What Is Blockchain?
summary: This article defines blockchain as a decentralized ledger of shared data, explaining how its cryptographic hashes and peer-to-peer network ensure data integrity, security, and immutability. It details the three main types of blockchain—public, private, and federated—and highlights the significant business benefits, including establishing trust, streamlining operations, and improving security, particularly when integrated with technologies like IoT and AI. The article also introduces Hyperledger as a key open-source initiative promoting enterprise blockchain solutions.

title: 6 Reasons Why Digital Brands Group Investors Are Smiling Today as DBGI Stock Soars
summary: Digital Brands Group (DBGI) stock soared on Tuesday following an updated guidance for fiscal year 2022, projecting revenue between $37.5 million and $42.5 million. This forecast represents a 350% increase from 2021 guidance and anticipates positive EBITDA, driven by expanded marketing, Amazon sales, new products, showrooms, and wholesale revenue. The company also plans for growth through acquisitions.

title: Turismo City se amplía y compró empresa brasilera Quanto Custa Viajar con una inversión de u$s6 millones
summary: Turismocity has expanded its operations by acquiring the Brazilian travel company Quanto Custa Viajar for $6 million. This investment round included participation from prominent executives like Eduardo Elsztain and Martin Migoya, aiming to solidify Turismocity's position as a leading global travel company. The acquisition follows Turismocity's earlier purchase of Farecompare and seeks to leverage synergies to grow its presence in the Brazilian market.

title: 1stDibs just released an e-commerce report. Here’s where they think online luxury is headed
summary: 1stDibs has released an e-commerce report highlighting the significant growth in the online luxury shopping market. The report indicates a substantial increase in 1stDibs's gross market value and active buyers, demonstrating the comfort consumers now have with purchasing high-value items online. While furniture remains its largest overall category, the company's highest individual sales are in art and jewelry, with a noteworthy average order value exceeding $2,500.

title: Lauren Hobart: age, children, husband, education, career, salary, profiles, net worth
summary: Lauren Hobart is the CEO of Dick's Sporting Goods, taking over in 2021 and driving significant growth and strategic planning for the company. With over 25 years in finance, retail, and consumer experience, she previously held various roles at Dick's, including Senior Vice President and CMO. Hobart has also been instrumental in initiatives like the Sports Matter program and successfully navigated the company through the 2020 economic and health crises, earning a reported compensation of over $6.7 million in 2019 and an estimated net worth of $46.5 million as of 2021.

title: Etsy debuts shoppable virtual house
summary: Etsy has launched "Etsy House," an interactive augmented reality experience allowing shoppers to tour a digital home decorated with marketplace items. This initiative builds on Etsy's previous AR offerings and positions it alongside other retailers like David's Bridal, Asos, and Amazon, who are utilizing AR and VR to enhance product visualization and e-commerce. The company has also recently expanded its business through acquisitions of Depop and Elo7.

title: Can LEO Meet the Changing Arctic’s Connectivity Needs?
summary: The Arctic's rapidly changing environmental and geopolitical landscape is increasing its strategic importance, driving a demand for enhanced connectivity. Low-Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites are emerging as a crucial solution to provide reliable communication in this data-starved region, where traditional Geostationary Orbit (GEO) satellites struggle. The U.S. government, through initiatives like the AFRL's DEUCSI program, is collaborating with commercial LEO operators such as Iridium, OneWeb, and SpaceX to deploy and test robust satellite communication capabilities for both military and commercial applications in the Arctic.

title: The Giant Company and Instacart launch grocery delivery in 30 minutes
summary: The Giant Company and Instacart have partnered to launch "Giant Instant Delivery" and "Martin’s Instant Delivery," offering grocery delivery in as fast as 30 minutes across Pennsylvania, Maryland, Virginia, and West Virginia. This service is part of Instacart’s "Convenience Hub" and competes with other rapid delivery options, including Kroger Delivery Now. The new offering aims to provide faster delivery windows and increased e-commerce convenience for shoppers, with an eye towards future growth with a new fulfillment center.

title: Capitalizing on the many artificial neural network uses
summary: This article explores the expanding uses of artificial neural networks (ANNs) in enterprises, highlighting their potential benefits despite challenges like ethical concerns and implementation complexities. It differentiates between convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for spatial data and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) for sequential data, providing examples such as facial recognition, medical analysis, fraud detection, and customer habit monitoring. The article also discusses crucial considerations for businesses, including addressing transparency issues, managing computational resources, and defining clear value statements before deployment.

title: Best Buy to Test Return-to-Office Plans Over the Holidays
summary: Best Buy will test its return-to-office plans over the holidays by asking a "small number of teams" to work from its Richfield corporate campus starting in November. This initiative will serve as a road test for the company's long-term hybrid work model, with all returning employees required to be vaccinated against Covid-19. Best Buy expects the majority of its corporate employees to return in early 2022, as many other Twin Cities companies have delayed their return-to-office plans.

title: HP’s Smartest Ink Tank Printer For People That Print A Lot
summary: HP Inc. has launched the new low-cost HP Smart Tank 7000 series printer, designed for individuals with high-volume printing needs. This series emphasizes sustainability, being HP's first ink tank printer made from over 25% recycled plastic, and offers smart features like self-healing Wi-Fi, automatic two-sided printing, and a spill-free refill system. The printers are available in the U.S. priced at USD$399 – $499.

title: Quick on Their Fleet: Kodiak Builds Flexible, High-Performance Self-Driving Trucks on NVIDIA DRIVE
summary: Kodiak Robotics has unveiled its fourth-generation self-driving truck, powered by NVIDIA DRIVE Orin. The trucks feature a lightweight mapping strategy and a discreet, modular hardware design to achieve level 4 self-driving capabilities, focusing on flexibility and live perception rather than detailed pre-constructed maps. This approach addresses the high demand for delivery and the shortage of drivers in the trucking industry.

title: Amazon settles labor dispute with fired climate activists
summary: Amazon has reached a private settlement with two former web designers, Emily Cunningham and Maren Costa, who were allegedly fired for their workplace activism. The National Labor Relations Board had previously accused Amazon of unfair labor practices, stating that the employees' terminations violated legal protections for advocating workplace changes related to climate change and COVID-19 safety concerns for warehouse workers. The terms of the settlement, known as a "private non-board agreement," will not be disclosed to the public but await approval from a regional director of the labor board.

title: Amazon opens its first Thurston County distribution warehouse
summary: Amazon has opened its first fulfillment center in Thurston County, located in Lacey, Washington. The new facility will create 1,000 jobs and is one of three warehouses on a newly developed site. This marks a significant expansion for the e-commerce giant in the state.

title: Cathie Wood’s Ark Investment sells $270M worth of Tesla stake
summary: Cathie Wood’s Ark Investment Management sold over 340,000 shares of Tesla, worth nearly $270 million, across three of its exchange-traded funds. This move comes as a bond selloff impacted rate-sensitive technology stocks, leading to outflows from Ark's growth-focused funds. Despite the sale, Tesla remains Ark's largest holding, with Wood predicting its shares will reach $3,000.

title: PayPal’s Happy Returns partners with Staples
summary: PayPal's Happy Returns has partnered with Staples to offer in-person, box-free returns at over a thousand Staples stores across the U.S., starting in California. This collaboration will make return services accessible within 10 miles for 75% of Americans and aims to streamline the return process for online shoppers while increasing foot traffic for Staples. The move follows PayPal's acquisition of Happy Returns and reflects a broader trend of payment companies engaging in acquisitions within the returns space to address growing e-commerce return challenges.

title: Jabil expects to hit over $8B in net revenue in Q1 of 2022
summary: Jabil Inc. (NYSE: JBL) reported strong financial results for the fourth quarter and fiscal year, with net revenue of $7.4 billion and $29.3 billion respectively, despite supply chain challenges. Looking ahead to Q1 2022, the company projects net revenue between $8 billion and $8.6 billion, driven by its diversified business model and opportunities in vehicle electrification, connected healthcare, and infrastructure development. Jabil continues to work with major clients such as Amazon, Tesla, Apple, and Johnson & Johnson.

title: General Motors' Commercial EV Unit To Expand Vehicle Lineup, Add Verizon As Customer
summary: General Motors' BrightDrop electric commercial vehicle business is expanding its lineup with a second delivery van, the EV410, and has secured Verizon Communications Inc. as a customer for this new vehicle. The EV410, aimed at segments requiring smaller vehicles like grocery and telecommunications, will begin production in the second half of 2023 at GM's CAMI assembly plant in Canada. This move highlights GM's increased investment in electric and autonomous vehicles, recognizing the growing demand and financial benefits for commercial EV fleets.

title: INSIGHTS | Conservative investors are pairing portfolio with principles
summary: Tom Carter, a mutual fund executive, has launched the American Conservative Values ETF to allow conservative investors to align their portfolios with their principles, avoiding "woke" companies. The fund, which began in October and already manages over $28 million, aims to provide an option for individuals who wish to invest in companies that share their conservative values rather than those that engage in social and racial justice advocacy. This initiative reflects a broader movement where conservatives are using economic choices to "fight back" against companies perceived as aligning with liberal politics.

title: Sonos Beam (2021, 2nd Gen) review: Compact soundbar delivers plenty of clout
summary: The Sonos Beam (2nd Gen) is presented as an excellent compact soundbar that, despite sharing much of its architecture with its predecessor, notably adds virtual Dolby Atmos support, a new processor, and an updated aesthetic with a plastic grille. While it doesn't offer true Dolby Atmos like larger, pricier alternatives, its virtual surround sound experience is highly effective for its size, especially when paired with additional Sonos speakers. The soundbar also boasts a sleek design, extensive smart features including voice assistants and AirPlay 2, and numerous music streaming options, making it a versatile choice for enhancing both TV audio and general music listening.
